title: SSH Brute Force Credential Attack
description: High frequency of failed SSH login attempts detected on prod-api-03 from IP 198.51.100.42. System is currently accessible via username/password authentication.
attack_behavior: Brute-force SSH password spraying targeting root and admin accounts from a single source IP.
root_cause: Password-based SSH authentication was exposed on the public internet without rate limiting.
analyst_investigation: Log analysis reveals 4,200 failed SSH logins within a 5-minute window. CPU spikes on prod-api-03 matching login attempts.
resolution: IP 198.51.100.42 blocked via firewall. SSH service reconfigured: PasswordAuthentication set to no, PubkeyAuthentication set to yes. Rate limiting enabled via Fail2ban.
outcome: Successfully contained. Attack stopped immediately. SSH authenticated via key only.
analyst_notes: First SSH brute force incident of this quarter on this segment. Rate limiting and ssh key enforcement resolved it.
lessons_learned: Password authentication should be disabled by default on all production public-facing endpoints.

title: Credential Spraying Attack
description: Multiple authentication attempts detected from rotating IP addresses targeting database credentials on prod-db-02.
attack_behavior: Credential spraying across database administrator roles. IP addresses are rotating every few attempts to bypass standard IP-based blocks.
root_cause: Database management port (3306) open to public subnet with password authentication allowed.
analyst_investigation: Identified rotating IP subnet 203.0.113.0/24 attempting standard root passwords. Attempts are spread out to bypass simple firewall rules.
actions_attempted: IP blocking of individual source IPs
failed_actions: IP blocking of individual source IPs (attacker rotated IPs instantly)
resolution: Disabled public access to prod-db-02. Enforced VPN + key-based bastion authentication. Added rate-limit blocking for database login failures.
outcome: Resolved successfully. Public port blocked, and connections now secured behind bastion.
analyst_notes: IP blocking failed because the attacker rotated source IP addresses. Applying key-based authentication and rate limiting was the only effective solution.
lessons_learned: Never expose database ports directly. IP-only blocks are ineffective against rotating IP credential sprays.

title: Credential Spraying and Privilege Escalation
description: Multiple login attempts from rotating IP addresses followed by a successful auth and unusual privilege escalation (sudo access) activity on production-api.
attack_behavior: Attacker sprayed credentials from rotating IPs, gained low-level system access, then executed a local exploit to modify sudoers and create a backdoor service account.
root_cause: Weak credential access leading to system entry, combined with unpatched local kernel vulnerability allowing root access.
analyst_investigation: Audit logs show user 'web-app' logging in successfully from 192.0.2.106. Sudo log shows execution of a local exploit to add 'web-app' to sudoers.
failed_actions: IP block (attacker used rotating proxy IPs)
resolution: Isolated host from network. Revoked backdoor accounts. Reverted sudoers modification. Enabled key-based SSH only. Patched kernel vulnerability and redeployed container.
outcome: Host isolated and restored. Privilege escalation path resolved.
analyst_notes: Pattern matches credential attacks (INC-1042 and INC-1097), but escalates to a coordinated compromise. IP blocking alone would have failed.
lessons_learned: Credential attacks should be escalated immediately if rotating IPs or privilege escalation behaviors are observed.

title: Suspicious OAuth Token Authorization
description: Anomalous authorization grant request detected. Client ID 'external_read_sync' requested administrator scope bypass consent.
attack_behavior: OAuth token hijacking or client-credentials compromise attempt.
root_cause: Improper scope verification check in identity provider endpoint.
analyst_investigation: Traced token generation back to an internal service credential which was leaked in a public developer sandbox.
resolution: Revoked client credentials, enforced consent checks, rotated developer credentials.
outcome: Token revoked. Abuse prevented.
analyst_notes: Credential leak in sandbox allowed the attacker to attempt admin token generation.
lessons_learned: Enforce strict scope limits and ensure sandbox environments do not hold production-grade keys.

title: Partner Gateway API Abuse
description: partner-gateway API is receiving 500x normal requests with customized headers designed to bypass rate-limiting rules.
attack_behavior: API scraping and parameter pollution to extract customer data.
root_cause: API rate-limiter configuration allowed header-based user-agent overrides.
analyst_investigation: Requests targeting client metadata fields. Bypassing standard rate limits using wildcard user agents.
resolution: Blocked source IP. Updated Gateway to rate limit strictly by API Key client credentials rather than headers or IPs.
outcome: Scraping blocked. System stabilized.
analyst_notes: Rate limit should always tie back to client credentials.
lessons_learned: Rate limit APIs at the credential/token level, not by header IP or User-Agent.

title: Exposed Internal Dashboard sandbox
description: An internal developer dashboard is accessible on the public internet without login.
attack_behavior: Shodan scan discovered port 8080 exposed publicly.
root_cause: Security group configuration error during sandbox deployment.
analyst_investigation: Security group was set to 0.0.0.0/0 instead of corporate subnet.
successful_actions: Restrict security group to corporate subnet
resolution: Modified AWS Security Group rules to block 0.0.0.0/0. Restricted port 8080 access to corporate VPN CIDR.
outcome: Successfully contained. Access closed.
analyst_notes: Exposed dashboard did not contain production data, but had sandbox credentials. Sandbox rotated.
lessons_learned: Security groups must be audited continuously for public rules.

title: Anomalous File Encryption Activity
description: Rapid file rename operations detected on internal-fileshare-02. File extensions changing to '.locked'.
attack_behavior: Ransomware-like activity encrypting shares via standard Samba connection.
root_cause: User workstation infected with malware accessing corporate shares via mapped drive.
analyst_investigation: Identified workstation WS-9872 belonging to finance department executing fileshare changes.
failed_actions: Reboot fileshare (did not stop encryption, workstation just reconnected)
resolution: Isolated infected workstation WS-9872. Revoked user network sessions. Restored encrypted files from volume shadow copy (VSS) taken 2 hours prior.
outcome: Workstation isolated. Files restored with 0% data loss.
analyst_notes: Rebooting fileserver is ineffective because the workstation reconnects and resumes. Target workstation isolation is required.
lessons_learned: Volume shadow copies are vital. Workstation isolation is the priority when share encryption is detected.

title: SQL Injection in Login Endpoint
description: SQL injection attacks detected on customer-portal login page resulting in DB error dumps.
attack_behavior: Automated SQLmap scans trying to dump admin database schemas.
root_cause: Login input parameter was directly concatenated into SQL query.
analyst_investigation: Attacker successfully retrieved system version info, but table dump was blocked by database user permission limits.
resolution: Blocked attacker IPs. Refactored the login query to use parameterized prepared statements. Enabled WAF SQL Injection protection rules.
outcome: Vulnerability patched. WAF now blocks all test requests.
analyst_notes: Direct query refactoring is the proper fix; WAF provides defense-in-depth.
lessons_learned: Ensure parameterized queries are enforced in CI lint checks.

title: CI/CD Token Leakage
description: Continuous deployment service account token used to download files from S3 buckets from a non-AWS IP address.
attack_behavior: Credential leakage. Attacker found a build log with exposed environment variables.
root_cause: Travis CI build logs had public read permissions enabled and printed the deploy token.
analyst_investigation: Leaked token was exposed in build #412 logs. Attacker read the logs and issued API commands to AWS.
resolution: Revoked deploy_key_77 credentials. Deleted the public build log. Re-configured CI to mask secrets dynamically.
outcome: Token revoked and rotated. Build log deleted.
analyst_notes: S3 access log shows only 4 non-sensitive files were downloaded.
lessons_learned: Always mask environment variables in build output configs.

title: Mass PDF Download from HR System
description: Standard employee account downloading all salary and review documents in quick succession.
attack_behavior: Data exfiltration by internal employee prior to resignation.
root_cause: Lack of rate limiting and lack of behavioral alerts on document downloads.
analyst_investigation: User 'jsmith' downloaded 820 resumes/reviews. Employee had submitted resignation 4 days ago.
actions_attempted: IP blocking (failed - user was on corporate VPN)
resolution: Disabled user Active Directory account to stop downloads. Notified HR and legal teams.
outcome: Account disabled. Data exfiltration stopped.
analyst_notes: IP block was ineffective because user used VPN IP. Disabling the AD user account immediately cut all access.
lessons_learned: Account disabling is the primary defense for insider risk. Set download alert thresholds.

title: Privilege Escalation on Kubernetes Node
description: A pod running in dev namespace successfully broke out of container boundaries to access root hostPID.
attack_behavior: Container breakout exploiting permissive securityContext configurations.
root_cause: Kubernetes Pod Security Policy was not enforced, allowing privileged containers to deploy.
analyst_investigation: Pod 'test-admin' was deployed with hostNetwork: true and privileged: true by a developer.
successful_actions: Implement OPA Gatekeeper policy blocking privileged container deployments
resolution: Deleted offending pod. Configured Open Policy Agent (OPA) rules to reject pod specs with hostPID, hostNetwork, or privileged: true.
outcome: Breach contained. Prevention policy enforced.
analyst_notes: Developer did not do this maliciously, but it exposes container escape vulnerabilities.
lessons_learned: Always enforce Pod Security Standards (PSS) at the cluster level.

title: OAuth Token Leak via Redirect URI
description: Suspicious login attempts using tokens leaked via open redirect parameter in OAuth login flow.
attack_behavior: Attacker registered a redirect_uri with wildcard (e.g., *.attacker.com) to intercept auth tokens.
root_cause: Validation library allowed wildcard matches on redirected URIs.
analyst_investigation: OAuth logs show client 'web-client' using redirect_uri targeting 'attacker.com/oauth/callback'.
resolution: Removed wildcard matches from client configuration database. Restricted redirect URIs to absolute matching paths.
outcome: Successfully resolved. Wildcard redirections closed.
analyst_notes: Strict redirect validation is critical in OAuth protocols.
lessons_learned: Never allow wildcard or open redirects in client authentication registries.

title: API Key Exposure in GitHub Public Repo
description: Github alerted security team that partner-gateway key part_key_03 was committed to a public repository.
attack_behavior: Accidental code leak by vendor team.
root_cause: Developer committed vendor config file to public github repository instead of using env variables.
analyst_investigation: Commit occurred 3 hours prior to alert. Key was active.
successful_actions: Run GitGuardian scanner on vendor repos
resolution: Revoked part_key_03. Provisioned new key and delivered it securely via Secrets Manager. Notified vendor developer.
outcome: Key rotated. Repo cleaned.
analyst_notes: Fast containment due to GitHub Token Scanning integration.
lessons_learned: Enforce pre-commit secrets scanning for all internal and vendor developers.

title: Ransomware Infection in Staging Cluster
description: File share files encrypted. Shadow copies deleted via vssadmin utility.
attack_behavior: Ransomware attack attempting to destroy local backup recovery points.
root_cause: Staging server compromised via local service vulnerability with root/SYSTEM privilege access.
analyst_investigation: VSS backups were successfully deleted. WORKSTATION WS-211 identified as source.
successful_actions: Restore files from remote cold storage backups
resolution: Isolated infected hosts. Disconnected network. Restored files from offsite cold storage backups.
outcome: Staging files restored. Local backup strategy updated.
analyst_notes: Since local shadow copies were deleted, remote backup restoration was the only option. Take longer than local restoration.
lessons_learned: Protect volume shadow copies against unauthorized deletion, and maintain write-once (WORM) offsite backups.

title: Exposed Prometheus Metrics Server
description: Dev sandboxed metrics server exposed port 9090 to public web search crawlers.
attack_behavior: Security crawler indexed public metrics revealing host names and system stats.
root_cause: Docker network binding configuration bound port 9090 to 0.0.0.0 instead of 127.0.0.1.
analyst_investigation: No credentials exposed, but infrastructure naming conventions leaked.
resolution: Re-configured docker-compose binding from '9090:9090' to '127.0.0.1:9090:9090' to restrict access to localhost only.
outcome: Exposed service closed. Metrics now private.
analyst_notes: Quick configuration fix. docker bindings must be monitored.
lessons_learned: Bind services to localhost unless public exposure is explicitly required and authenticated.

title: Credential Stuffing on Customer Login API
description: 50,000 login attempts against customer account login endpoint. Heavy failure rate using credential stuffing list.
attack_behavior: Automated login attempts using credentials leaked from external database breaches.
root_cause: Customer login API lacked Captcha or device-based rate-limiting controls.
analyst_investigation: Attacker rotating across 10,000 proxy IPs. Blocks on single IPs were ineffective.
actions_attempted: Single IP blocking (failed due to massive IP proxy list)
successful_actions: Global rate limit per customer username
resolution: Enabled rate limit restricting login attempts per account to 3 per minute. Enforced Cloudflare interactive challenge mode for authentication requests.
outcome: Stuffing attack mitigated. Login error rates normalized.
analyst_notes: IP blocking failed due to rotating proxy list. Username rate limiting and Captcha resolved the issue.
lessons_learned: IP blocks are ineffective against credential stuffing. Enforce username-based rate limits and CAPTCHA challenge-response.

title: SQL Injection in Search API
description: Time-based SQL injection detected on search gateway query parameters.
attack_behavior: Attacker trying to trigger database latency sleep() commands to verify blind injection point.
root_cause: SQL query was dynamically constructed with unsanitized parameters.
analyst_investigation: Confirmed SQL injection vulnerabilities in partner query endpoint. Attacker did not retrieve tables.
resolution: Refactored raw SQL query structure to utilize parameterized input bindings via SQLAlchemy ORM.
outcome: Blind SQL injection resolved.
analyst_notes: Raw queries refactored into modern ORM structures to remove injection points.
lessons_learned: Enforce SQL parameters or ORMs across all backend repository files.

title: OAuth Token Replay Attack
description: Attacker attempted to reuse authorization codes to obtain access tokens multiple times.
attack_behavior: OAuth code interception and replay attempt.
root_cause: Authorization codes were not invalidated after first use in the token exchange endpoint.
analyst_investigation: Code 'auth_code_982' was exchanged twice. Second exchange succeeded due to database cache lookup lag.
resolution: Updated token service to immediately delete authorization codes from cache upon token exchange request, prior to token validation.
outcome: Token replay prevented. OAuth specs strictly enforced.
analyst_notes: OAuth codes must be single-use. Cache latency was resolved.
lessons_learned: Enforce single-use token exchange and handle high-concurrency race conditions in auth cache.

title: SSH Key Leak in Public Wiki
description: Internal wiki documentation page contained a copy-pasted SSH private key used for prod-api-03 backup sync.
attack_behavior: Exposed credential. Key visible to all company staff and external vendors.
root_cause: Analyst shared credential in documentation for setup convenience.
analyst_investigation: Audit logs for prod-api-03 SSH logins checked. No unauthorized logins found. Key leaked in wiki 18 days ago.
successful_actions: Revoke SSH public key on host
resolution: Revoked authorized key on prod-api-03. Generated new keypair. Restructured wiki page, masked keys. Deleted wiki revision history containing key.
outcome: SSH Key rotated and revoked. Security hygiene audit scheduled.
analyst_notes: Quick response. Wikis should be audited regularly for keys.
lessons_learned: Private keys must never be stored in wiki documentations. Use secrets managers.

title: DDoS Attack on API Gateway
description: Massive volume of GET requests targeting /v1/status endpoint, causing gateway timeout.
attack_behavior: Distributed denial of service targeting resource-intensive status APIs.
root_cause: Status endpoint performed complex backend health checks without cache, amplifying database load.
analyst_investigation: 1.2 million requests/min. Database connection pool exhausted.
actions_attempted: IP blocking (failed - traffic came from botnet)
successful_actions: Enable DDoS protection profile in Cloudflare
resolution: Implemented 60-second caching on health status results. Enabled Cloudflare DDoS protection rules. Restricted DB connections.
outcome: DDoS mitigated. API gateway returned to service. Status checks now cached.
analyst_notes: IP blocking failed since the traffic was highly distributed. Caching status endpoints resolved database exhaustion.
lessons_learned: Health/status check APIs must be heavily cached and isolated from database connection dependencies.

title: S3 Bucket Public Read Permission
description: An S3 bucket holding development database backups was set to public read access.
attack_behavior: Security researcher scanned open buckets and detected backup files.
root_cause: CloudFormation template default values allowed public read permissions on developer buckets.
analyst_investigation: No evidence of malicious download, but database backups contained user testing hashes.
resolution: Enabled AWS Account-level Block Public Access. Applied bucket policy restricting access. Enabled server-side KMS encryption.
outcome: Bucket public access closed. Backups encrypted.
analyst_notes: AWS configuration correction. Policies updated.
lessons_learned: Enable account-wide 'Block Public Access' policies in AWS by default.

title: Workstation Ransomware Isolation
description: Cryptowall ransomware running on workstation WS-145 modifying mounted network shares.
attack_behavior: Ransomware encryption spreading from localized workspace.
root_cause: User downloaded email attachment containing payload.
analyst_investigation: Malware detected by endpoint defense on WS-145, but fileshare mount encryption was already in progress.
resolution: Isolated WS-145 workstation. Reverted fileshare modifications using shadow copy rollback.
outcome: Contained successfully. Workstation isolated.
analyst_notes: Targeted host isolation prevented major share encryption. Files restored.
lessons_learned: ワークステーション(workstation) endpoints must be isolated immediately rather than server restarts.

title: SSH Credential spraying prod
description: Failed root credentials spray attempts on prod-api-03 SSH port.
attack_behavior: Low-frequency ssh credential spraying.
root_cause: SSH password-based access was active, allowing root password trials.
analyst_investigation: 150 attempts. Blocked source IP. Checked configuration.
resolution: Blocked IP 198.51.100.12. Enabled Fail2ban with 3 login failures lockout policy.
outcome: Contained. Key SSH setup was not active during this incident.
analyst_notes: IP blocking helped, but password access remains active. System needs key-based conversion.
lessons_learned: Enforce key-based authentication on all prod ports.

title: Admin Credential Abuse
description: Unauthorized admin database user login from Tor exit node IP.
attack_behavior: Leaked database credential usage.
root_cause: Database admin password was weak and reused on other services.
analyst_investigation: Tor node IP accessed db metrics schema. Credential rotated.
actions_attempted: IP block (failed due to rotating Tor exit nodes)
resolution: Rotated admin DB passwords. Disabled public database direct routing. Enforced SSH VPN bastion.
outcome: Secure access enforced. Key credentials rotated.
analyst_notes: IP blocking failed since Tor exits change instantly. Rotated credentials and closed ports.
lessons_learned: Direct database admin access from internet must be disabled. Enforce bastion tunnels.

title: Privilege escalation via dirtycow
description: User execution of local exploit binaries targeting outdated kernel version.
attack_behavior: Local privilege escalation attempting to bypass container boundaries.
root_cause: System kernel version was outdated and vulnerable to Dirty COW (CVE-2016-5195).
analyst_investigation: A compromised low-privilege docker service was used to execute host shell exploits.
resolution: Terminated compromised container. Patched host Linux kernel to latest version. Rebooted node.
outcome: Kernel updated. Exploitation closed.
analyst_notes: Patched kernel version resolved local exploit path.
lessons_learned: Perform regular automated kernel patch management across cluster hosts.
